questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to become a professional football player
The culture of fan communities and the words they use
Why people stop supporting their favourite teams
The history of Hollywood movie stars
questions.why: Beth says they are taking a trip into the world of fandoms, which has started to develop its own language.

questions.q: According to Neil, what helped create the idea of 'fandom'?
options: The internet, which lets fans meet and share
TV shows that brought sports fans together
New books and magazines written by fans
Football clubs selling tickets online
questions.why: Neil says that thanks to the internet, fans around the world can meet online, and this led to the word 'fandom'.

questions.q: Why can being a fan on your own be difficult, according to Michael Bond?
options: Buying fan items alone costs a lot of money
Nobody around you wants to talk about it
It can look odd and people may laugh at you
Fan clubs don't accept single members
questions.why: He says fan pursuits can look quirky, odd or obsessive, and you often get mocked.

questions.q: What example does Michael Bond give of something hard to do alone in public?
options: Singing football songs in the street
Dressing as a Harry Potter character at work
Watching Disney cartoons in a cinema
Wearing Regency-era clothes as a Jane Austen fan
questions.why: He says a Jane Austen fan dressing in a bonnet and gown would find it hard to do alone in public.

questions.q: Who, according to Michael Bond, likes to invent terms such as BIRGing and CORFing?
options: Football players
Academics who study fandoms
Sports journalists
Young fans on social media
questions.why: He says academics who study fandoms love to use acronyms to describe football fans' behaviour.

questions.q: What do football fans typically do when their team loses and they are CORFing?
options: Celebrate in the streets anyway
Say that they personally lost the game
Buy more tickets for the next match
Distance themselves and blame the players
questions.why: Neil says instead of saying “WE won!”, they say “THEY played rubbish!”

questions.q: What does Beth say about 'true fans'?
options: They never distance themselves from their team
They only support teams that win
They usually stop watching after many losses
They prefer online fandoms to real matches
questions.why: Beth says, “Of course, true fans never CORF.”

questions.q: Why does Beth mention fans whose team loses week after week?
options: To show that fans always prefer winning teams
To explain why football is becoming less popular
To show some fans oddly enjoy their team losing
To suggest that those fans should change teams
questions.why: She says some fans take a kind of strange pessimistic pleasure when their team loses.
